transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Lately I can’t stop dwelling on how my face and body look as I’m aging, and it’s making me avoid things I used to do without thinking. I'm just feeling really overwhelmed by it all, and it's getting harder to just go about my day.
Did these worries start after a specific stressful life event or change, or have they been a long-standing concern about your appearance?

I've always cared about my appearance, but these worries got much worse recently as I started going through perimenopause and my kids became more independent. Around the same time, I took on a more public-facing role at my law office, doing community workshops and appearing in newsletters. Being so visible suddenly made me feel incredibly self-conscious about how much I'm aging.
Have these appearance worries become the main thing you think about each day, or do you also worry a lot about many other areas of life like work, family, money, and health?

It is definitely my appearance that takes up almost all of my thoughts. I don't really worry about things like money or my family's health; instead, my mind is constantly fixed on how my face and neck are drooping and looking worn-out. Even when I worry about work or social events, the root of it is always the fear of how other people will judge how I look.
Do you find yourself doing things like repeatedly checking mirrors, comparing your appearance to others, seeking reassurance, or trying to hide or fix the parts of your appearance that worry you?

Yes, I do. Most mornings I spend almost an hour in front of the mirror putting on and wiping off makeup, tilting my head, and zooming in on my face with my phone camera. I also constantly change outfits to hide my neck and arms, and I keep repeatedly asking my husband if I look too old.

Do you also have unwanted, intrusive thoughts or urges about things like contamination, checking, symmetry, or harming someone, and do you feel driven to do repetitive rituals to reduce that anxiety? Or is the concern mainly about your appearance and aging?

No, I don't have any worries about contamination, symmetry, or hurting anyone. My concerns are entirely focused on my face sagging and my neck drooping, and any repetitive habits I have are strictly tied to how old I look.
Do you believe there is definitely something wrong or ugly about your appearance that other people can see, or do you recognize that these worries may be exaggerated and mostly in your own mind?

Even though my husband and coworkers tell me they don't notice anything, I find it incredibly hard to believe them. To me, the sagging lines and my drooping neck are so prominent that I truly believe everyone must be noticing how old and worn-out I look, even if they are just trying to be polite.

Do you ever get intrusive, unwanted thoughts or images that are not about your appearance, and feel driven to do repetitive actions to relieve the anxiety they cause? Or are your repetitive behaviors only about checking or hiding how you look?

No, I don't have any unrelated intrusive thoughts or feel driven to do rituals like checking locks or washing my hands. Everything I do is strictly about my appearance and trying to check, hide, or fix how old and worn-out I look. It is completely focused on my face and neck.
When you look at your face or neck, do you believe there is definitely something wrong that others can see, or do you think the concern might be exaggerated and mostly in your own mind?

Even though my husband and coworkers tell me I look fine, I can't shake the feeling that they're just being polite. When I look in the mirror, the sagging lines and my drooping neck look so obvious that I truly believe everyone is noticing how old and worn-out I look. It feels far too real to just be in my head.

Do you feel your concern is mainly that you look unattractive or deformed to others, or do you also have intrusive, unwanted thoughts and rituals that go beyond appearance, like checking or mental counting, to reduce anxiety?

Yes, my concern is entirely about looking unattractive, old, and worn-out to other people. I don't have any unrelated thoughts or rituals like mental counting or checking things. Any habits I have, like zooming in with my phone or asking my husband for reassurance, are strictly focused on how my face and neck look.

opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The presentation is most consistent with body dysmorphic disorder: persistent preoccupation with perceived facial/neck aging and defects, repetitive mirror checking/reassurance seeking/camouflaging, poor insight with near-delusional conviction, and clear distress/avoidance with functional impact. Symptoms are narrowly focused on appearance rather than multiple life domains, arguing against generalized anxiety, and there are no non-appearance obsessions/compulsions to suggest primary OCD.
